column2: Jonathan's proposal to his equipment bearer is to cross to the messab on the other side; his failure to tell his father remains explicit. The opaque station term is retained.
Saul sits at the hill's summit beneath Magdon's pomegranate tree with about six hundred men; the selected tree, locality and number remain.
Ahijah's genealogy through Ahitub, brother of Jochabed, Phinehas and Eli remains, together with priesthood at Shiloh, the ephoud and the people's ignorance of Jonathan's departure.
column3: The genitives attach brother to Ahitub; Jochabed is the selected form, not silently changed to Ichabod. The inherited comma sequence requires attentive reading.

column2: The crossing toward the foreigners' station lies between rocky promontories named Bazes and Senna; both sides and names remain distinct.
The two roads are described by north toward Michmash and south toward Geba; selected road terminology is not replaced by a description of cliffs from another text.
The repeated crossing proposal names the uncircumcised and tentatively hopes for divine action, grounded in the Lord's freedom to save through many or few. Perhaps preserves the tentativeness.
The bearer supports everything Jonathan's heart inclines toward and says Here I am with you, my heart as yours. The doubled heart image remains.
Propose restoring Behold before the plan to cross and roll down toward the men. The unusual rolling verb remains rather than an unmarked substitution of show ourselves.
If told to stay until further instruction, they will stand on their own and certainly not ascend; the strong negative and first branch of the sign remain.
The alternative invitation triggers ascent because the Lord has delivered them into our hands; the sign is identified explicitly. The inherited But makes the contrast between branches audible.
Both enter the messab, and the foreigners' Behold introduces their interpretation of Hebrews emerging from hiding holes. Their reported perspective remains.
The invitation promises to let the pair know a word; Jonathan then tells his bearer to ascend after him because the Lord has delivered the enemies into Israel's hands.
column3: The threatening implication of letting them know is left in the speech rather than expanded into an explicit attack promise.

column2: Jonathan climbs on hands and feet with the bearer; enemies look him in the face, he strikes them and the bearer continues behind. No added finishing-off action is assigned to the bearer.
The first blow by Jonathan and his bearer concerns about twenty men, followed by darts, stone-throwers and pebbles of the plain.
column3: The weapon/stone phrase remains difficult in syntax and vocabulary; it is not replaced by a half-acre measure from a different source.

column2: Terror spans camp, field, messab people and destroyers, with unwillingness to act, the astonished earth and terror from the Lord all retained.
column3: Astonishment is not silently converted into a geological earthquake description; the personified earth and human fear may overlap without being identical statements.

column2: Propose restoring the looked-and-behold structure at the discovery of the camp's turmoil; this way and that preserves the repeated directional expression.
Propose restoring behold at the muster's discovery that Jonathan and his bearer were absent. The request to identify who has gone and the executed muster remain.
Ahijah is told to bring the ephoud, and its bearing before Israel that day supplies the explanation; the object is not changed to the ark.
The noise keeps increasing while Saul speaks, then Saul tells the priest to withdraw his plural hands. The progressive growth and plural body part remain.
Propose Behold before the discovered mutual sword fighting. Saul and the people's cry and movement to battle precede the greatly confused scene.
Slaves formerly with the foreigners in camp turn to Israel with Saul and Jonathan; the yesterday-and-third-day idiom is rendered previously, not an exact two-day chronology.
Israelites hiding on Ephraim's hill hear of the flight and join behind for battle; both hearing and ensuing pursuit remain.
Divine saving is followed by the complete selected continuation: battle beyond Baithon, about ten thousand with Saul and fighting spread through the city in Ephraim's hill country.

Propose separating the coordinated vengeance declaration from the evening prohibition: the Greek says and I will avenge, whereas inherited until I take vengeance creates an additional temporal condition. Great ignorance, the curse and universal non-tasting remain.
column3: The new sentence boundary is an English presentation choice; it preserves coordination without claiming ancient punctuation or approval of Saul's oath.

column2: All the land eating a meal remains before the iaar, described as a wooded bee-place facing the field.
column3: Iaar and the compressed wooded/bee-place construction remain opaque; land may stand for its inhabitants, but no new actor is inserted.

column2: Propose restoring the second presentative with behold before no one returned his hand to his mouth. There he was already carries the first; fear of the Lord's oath remains the cause.
column3: The singular going-and-speaking subject is unnamed and unresolved, and the relation to the collective people is not silently repaired.

column2: Jonathan's ignorance of the oath precedes staff-tip dipping, hand returning to mouth and his eyes looking up. No explanation of eye brightening or bodily recovery replaces the selected verb.
A member of the people reports the emphatic oath with today's prohibition; the separate narration of the people's exhaustion remains outside the inner quotation.
Jonathan understands and says his father has dismissed the land, then points to his seeing eyes after tasting a little honey.
column3: Dismissed for apellachen is provisional and unusual; it is not replaced without evidence by troubled. The source's seeing repetition is retained.

column2: Propose But at the conditional counterclaim: free eating from the found enemy spoils would have produced a greater blow now. Freely renders the emphatic eating expression without adding a new quantity.
A singular actor strikes some foreigners at Michmash that day and the people grow very weary; the actor remains he rather than an unsupported plural subject.
Turning to spoil, taking flocks, cattle and calves, slaughtering on the ground and eating with the blood remain distinct steps. No explanation is supplied in place of the stated blood issue.
The report names sin against the Lord through blood eating, and Saul at Geththem commands a large stone to be rolled to him.
column3: Geththem is retained as the selected location rather than converted into an accusation such as you have dealt treacherously.

column2: Propose preserving each person's singular hand in the final bringing clause. Dispersal, each calf and sheep, slaughter upon this and the emphatic prevention of sin through blood eating remain.
column3: Upon this points to the preceding stone contextually; no new sacrificial apparatus is inserted.

column2: Saul's building an altar and the repeated beginning-to-build statement both remain; this is not simply recast as his first altar without noting the selected verbal wording.
Saul proposes night pursuit, plunder until dawn and leaving no man; the assent is followed by the priest's call to approach God. The exterminating proposal is retained without embellishment.
The inquiry asks about descent and divine handing over, with Wilt Thou appropriate to direct singular address. God's non-answer that day remains an explicit negative.
The call to Israel's chiefs introduces knowing and seeing in whom today's sin occurred; chiefs is a contextual rendering of corners, not a lexical identity claim.
Propose For at the oath's opening to retain its explanatory connection to the inquiry. Divine saving, a possible answer against Jonathan, certain death and the people's complete silence remain.
Both the people and Saul with Jonathan will be in servitude; the repeated selected word remains despite its difficulty in the lot procedure.
column3: Douleia is not silently rendered one side/other side; whether the expression has a specialized procedural force remains unresolved.

column2: The full prayer preserves non-answer, two possible locations of wrongdoing, repeated divine title, clear signs and holiness, then selection of Jonathan and Saul and release of the people.
column3: The inherited indirect if Thou sayest it is in Thy people is an editorial construal of the embedded saying, not ancient punctuation evidence; free interprets the people's going out in the lot context. Technical identification of the lot terms remains open.

column2: Saul demands a lot between father and son and death for the selected one; the people's refusal, Saul's prevailing, the casting and Jonathan's selection all remain.
column3: This must not be expresses the people's rejection of the word; the longer selected objection and coercion sequence is not omitted.

column2: Jonathan answers the demand with emphatic tasting, a little honey at his staff tip and Here I am, I am dying. Present dying remains without changing the speech into a question.
Saul's self-imprecatory oath and certainly dying today remain; still more conveys the added-action curse formula without naming an unstated punishment.
The people challenge today's execution, swear that no hair will fall, speak of God's people working this day and pray for Jonathan, who does not die.
column3: The negative oath uses ei in its oath construction, not a positive prediction; the difficult people-have-worked-the-day clause is provisional. Prayed is not changed to ransomed.

column2: Saul goes up from pursuit and the foreigners go to their own place; the reciprocal departure ends the scene without an added peace agreement.
Saul is allotted a task over Israel, fights the full enemy list including Baitheor, and is delivered wherever he turns. The passive delivered is not replaced by active punishing enemies.
Mighty action, striking Amalek and rescuing Israel from those trampling it remain; the bodily oppression image is retained.
Jonathan, Jessiu and Melchisa remain the three sons, with Merab firstborn daughter and Michal second. Selected name forms are not harmonized against another genealogy.
Ahinoam's father Ahimaaz and commander Abner son of Ner, son of Saul's relative, remain.
column3: The repeated son chain follows the selected syntax; relative is not narrowed to uncle without further evidence.

column2: Kish is identified as Saul's father; Ner as Abner's father, Jamin's son and Abiel's grandson follows the inherited attachment of the chain.
column3: The scope of the final genealogical apposition is open; no harmonization with verse 50 or another book is claimed.

column2: Fierce war lasts all Saul's days, and every mighty man or son of might he sees is gathered to him. The two descriptions and continuing recruitment remain.
